summary:
Allwork.Space reports on Savills' Q2 2026 State of the U.S. Office Market, which finds the U.S. office market continuing its post-pandemic recovery through the first half of 2026. Leasing activity totaled 127.3 million square feet in the first six months, up 13% year over year and the strongest first-half performance since before the pandemic, exceeding every post-pandemic first-half total.

Demand remains concentrated in premium, best-in-class buildings, as companies focus on leasing high-quality space. That concentration is tightening availability at the top of the market and supporting rent growth for the highest-quality properties.

Conditions improved broadly: 82% of tracked U.S. office markets reported lower availability than a year earlier, and another 9% were largely unchanged.

Investment activity also strengthened, with office investment volume up 15% year over year, indicating better market liquidity despite a slower second quarter.

These gains occurred against a softening macroeconomic backdrop: GDP growth eased to 1.5%, inflation held at 3.5%, and payroll growth moderated. The piece concludes that continued lease signing suggests office demand has proven resilient despite economic uncertainty.

The article is a short market-data brief with no discussion of workplace operations, hybrid policy specifics, hot desking, or workplace technology tooling.
